source.title: From Data Quality to Model Quality: An Exploratory Study on Deep Learning
source.authors: Tian-Xing He; Sheng-Cheng Yu; Zi-Yuan Wang; Jie-Qiong Li; Zhen-Yu Chen

record.tranche_reason: Tests the effect of randomized label corruption on the same image-classification behavior, but uses partial-corruption sweeps rather than the original fully random-label intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper reports label-corruption outcomes for MNIST and CIFAR-10. Its general setup says models are trained until training accuracy reaches 100%, but it does not give condition-specific training-accuracy results for corrupted-label settings. Gaussian noise, salt-and-pepper noise, brightness, contrast, class deletion, and dataset-size results do not measure the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study varies random training-label corruption and measures classification accuracy, using the same basic intervention and outcome as the original experiments. Its reported results bear on V4, although condition-specific memorization outcomes are unavailable.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors regard label errors as especially harmful, describe CIFAR-10 corruption above 20% as intolerable, and report MNIST test accuracy of 10% at 15% corruption. These conclusions concern test performance, not demonstrated failure or success in memorizing corrupted labels.
record.recipe_differences: Uses random label changes at varying fractions on MNIST and CIFAR-10 rather than the original fully random-label intervention; reports test accuracy rather than a fully specified training-error and test-error comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and label-corruption fraction affect the reported outcomes.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The text gives only qualitative CIFAR-10 corruption outcomes and does not report condition-specific training accuracy for the corrupted-label experiments.
record.rows_left_out: No other label-corruption results were stated in text with assignable numeric outcomes; plotted curves in Figs. 6–9 are not transcribed into additional rows. Other data-quality interventions do not bear on the listed versions.

untested.parts: Fully corrupted MNIST labels are included in the experimental design, but successful near-zero training error, chance test performance at full corruption, stochastic-gradient details, and unchanged hyperparameters are not established by the supplied results.
Relative training time and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or wholly Gaussian-noise inputs. Adding noise to existing images does not test these conditions.
Condition-specific perfect training fit and a readable full corruption-response curve; CIFAR-10 corruption is tested only through 60%.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Separate learning trajectories for real-label patterns and noisy examples. An early test-accuracy peak followed by decline does not directly establish their learning order.

record.verdict_notes: The training-to-100% statement specifies intended procedure rather than condition-specific achieved results. R2 and R3 warrant no verdict about smooth degradation from the available qualitative descriptions. Additional plotted curves are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing. The figures themselves are unavailable in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: The paper varies the fraction of randomly changed labels, including 100% for MNIST, but reports no condition-specific training error or explicit outcome for fully random labels; the CIFAR-10 sweep stops at 60%.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed by label-corruption fraction.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input fitting experiment.
The paper does not report that training accuracy remains perfect at each corruption fraction; its stated result concerns testing accuracy.
No weight-decay, dropout, or data-augmentation comparison.
No analysis of training order or whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy labels.

rows.subject: lenet-5
rows.operation_detail: Trained with randomly modified MNIST training labels; the paper describes the test-accuracy outcome.
rows.note: The paper says this equals the expected value of random judgment. Its setup says models are trained until training-set accuracy reaches 100%, but does not state the training accuracy for this specific condition.
rows.check: The reported 10% test accuracy at only 15% corruption indicates an early collapse to chance, rather than establishing the full smooth-degradation claim. The general training-to-100% statement is a stopping rule, not a reported training-accuracy result for this condition.

source_check.locator_found: Experiment setup, lines 112–138; Results for RQ3, lines 181–187; Fig. 7 caption, line 209.

rows.subject: Resnet-20
rows.operation_detail: Trained with randomly modified CIFAR-10 training labels; the paper describes the test-accuracy curve.
rows.value: Not higher than the highest accuracy rate at the beginning of training
rows.note: The paper says accuracy declines after a steep increase at the beginning; the stated outcome is qualitative and does not establish chance test error.
rows.check: The value describes test accuracy declining over training within corrupted-label conditions. It does not establish the shape of test error across corruption fractions or perfect training fit. Figure 8 includes training accuracy, but its curves cannot be read from the supplied text.

rows.subject: NIN network
rows.operation_detail: Trained with randomly modified CIFAR-10 training labels; the paper describes the test-accuracy outcome.
rows.value: More than 20% error labels are intolerable
rows.note: The paper says the accuracy also shows this outcome for NIN, without giving a numeric value or specifying chance performance.
rows.check: The authors' characterization of corruption above 20% as intolerable supplies neither an accuracy value nor a comparison sufficient to establish smooth degradation or perfect training fit.

relationships.condition: LeNet-5 on MNIST with 15% randomly incorrect training labels
relationships.reason: R1 reports chance-level test accuracy of 10% already at 15% corruption, qualifying the proposed gradual degradation while substantial label signal remains; perfect training fit is unverified.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy fell to the 10% chance level already at 15% corruption.

relation.reason: Its own experiments vary random training-label corruption and measure test accuracy, directly bearing on V4's degradation component.

tranche.reason: The study conducts its own random wrong-label corruption experiment on data quality. Its results address V4, but the text does not establish replication of the original fitting protocol or report condition-specific training-error outcomes needed to justify T1.

source_check.notes: The setup states a training target of 100% accuracy, without reporting its attainment for R1. The RQ3 paragraph references both fixed-zero and random-label figures; the random-corruption setup and Fig. 7 support the recorded condition.
